subtopics.title: The Magnetic Field of a Current and the Right Hand Rule

questions.question: The magnetic field surrounding a long straight current-carrying wire is made of:
options: Concentric circles around the wire, tighter near the wire
Straight lines running parallel to the wire
Nothing — a straight wire has no field

questions.question: In the Right Hand Rule for a straight wire, the thumb and curled fingers stand for:
options: Thumb the field, fingers the current
Thumb the conventional current, fingers the circular field direction
Thumb the force, fingers the velocity

questions.question: Inside a current-carrying solenoid the magnetic field is:
options: Strong, nearly uniform, and directed along the axis

questions.question: A scrapyard crane lifts cars with an electromagnet rather than a permanent magnet because:
options: Switching the current off releases the load — a permanent magnet never lets go

subtopics.title: Magnetic Flux — Counting Field Through a Surface

questions.question: Magnetic flux is calculated as:
options: Φ = BA cosθ, with θ measured between the field and the normal to the surface
Φ = BA sinθ, with θ measured from the surface

questions.question: The flux through a surface reaches its MAXIMUM when the field:
options: Is perpendicular to the surface, lying along the normal
Lies in the plane of the surface

questions.question: A 0,02 m² coil sits in a 0,6 T field with its normal at 60° to the field. The flux is:
The unit of magnetic flux is the:

subtopics.title: Faraday's Law and the Direction of the Induced Current

questions.question: Faraday's law states that the magnitude of the induced emf is proportional to:
options: The steady flux through the coil
The strength of the magnet alone
The rate of change of magnetic flux through the conductor

questions.question: A powerful magnet is held perfectly still inside a coil. The induced current is:
options: Zero, because the flux through the coil is not changing

questions.question: A north pole approaches the face of a solenoid. The induced current turns that face into:
options: A south pole, to draw the magnet in faster
A north pole, to repel the approaching magnet

questions.question: If the induced current assisted the change instead of opposing it, the result would violate:
options: The law of conservation of energy
The law of conservation of charge

questions.question: A 150-turn coil of area 0,04 m², field along the normal, sees the field grow from 0,1 T to 0,5 T in 0,4 s. The emf magnitude is:
In ε = −NΔΦ/Δt, the quantity ΔΦ means:
options: The area swept out by the coil
The final flux minus the initial flux through one turn
The total flux through all N turns added together

questions.question: If that 6 V coil forms a closed circuit of total resistance 2,4 Ω, the induced current is:
Doubling the number of turns, with the same flux change over the same time:
Oersted's compass needle flinched when the current switched on because:
options: The current wrapped the wire in a magnetic field
The heat of the wire moved the air

questions.question: Winding a wire into a solenoid is useful because:
options: The stacked loop fields build a strong magnet with a north end and a south end
It traps the field so it cannot escape

questions.question: The decisive advantage an electromagnet holds over a bar magnet is that it:

subtopics.title: How Much Field Fits Through the Window?

questions.question: In the rain-and-bucket picture of flux, the rain, the mouth of the bucket and the tilt represent:
options: Field strength, area and the angle factor

questions.question: A loop turned fully edge-on to the magnetic field catches:
An enormous but perfectly steady flux through a coil generates:
options: No current at all — only a changing flux induces current

questions.question: For eleven years after Oersted, magnets resting beside coils generated nothing because:
options: The coils had too few turns
The magnets of the time were too weak
The missing ingredient was change — only a changing flux induces current

questions.question: Pushing the magnet into the coil faster makes the induced current:
options: Larger, because the flux changes at a greater rate

questions.question: The electrical energy delivered by an induced current ultimately comes from:
options: The magnet's stored magnetism, which slowly runs out
The work done pushing against the opposing induced effects

questions.question: A power station generator produces electricity by:
options: Holding strong magnets stationary inside huge coils
Spinning coils in magnetic fields so the flux through them changes continuously
